reason: This passage (Genesis 32-33) does not portray people from the elite unfavorably. The text centers on Jacob's spiritual journey and family reconciliation. While wealthy figures appear (Jacob with his substantial flocks and servants, Esau with his retinue of 400 men), neither is depicted negatively. Esau is portrayed sympathetically—emotional, forgiving, and generous, refusing excessive gifts. Jacob, despite his wealth, is shown as humble, prayerful, and spiritually earnest. The narrative's concerns are relational and theological rather than a critique of elite or wealthy people as a class. There is no explicit or implicit condemnation of the elite specifically.
